161.text:
I step on a truck.
The first two persons that I see are a driver and an aid.
The driver wears a uniform and the aid wears civies.
The former tells the latter to make room for me.
There are a lot of passengers too.
Most of them are young women traders.
They sit on two benches.
There is only one little boy sitting on his mother's thigh.
The mother seems tired and sleepy.
I am seated beside an ugly little old lady.
Her dark thin hands and foot as well as her pale anxious face let me know that she's a poor laboured rustic.
My eyes turn to the left and look at some girls in front of me.
They spread a small square blue plastic sheet on the floor of the truck.
The sheet is ragged and dirty, but it must replace a dining table.
Every girl takes out her box of food from her handbag and set it on the sheet.
The food includes cooked rice covered with Chinese peas.
There isn't any, piece of meat.
No chopsticks and spoons, the girls pick the food up by their fingers, like the habit of Cambodians.
After an hour and a half, the truck arrives at the terminal station.
Everybody gets down.
One, two, three, four rented honda drivers dart towards me.
One of them grasps my hand tightly to drag me to his Honda.
Frightened, anxious about losing my luggage, I try to leave there quickly.
